limits.value: rate USD 0.025/vCPU-hour and USD 0.015/GiB-hour; no egress terms published on the pages read

identity_cost.detail: A USD 50 credit is advertised; the card, hold and debit terms were not readable because the vendor pricing page did not render for a text read. Unverified.

record.confidence_note: The rates come from a third-party aggregator (boxyard.dev) that cites the vendor's own docs URL, and are consistent with the vendor homepage's meta description ('billed per second at $0.04/hr'). The vendor's pricing page returned a JavaScript stub on three routes (docs.isorun.ai/getting-started/pricing, its .md variant, isorun.ai/pricing), so no first-party quote of the rate exists.

evidence.proved: 'Every new account gets $50 in free credit, about 1,250 hours of a default sandbox. No card required to start.' with 'vCPU $0.025/hour', 'RAM $0.015/GiB/hour' and 'Hibernated sandboxes: not billed for active runtime; you pay nothing while the sandbox is paused', quoted
quoted: 'It costs $0.025 per vCPU-hour and $0.015 per GiB-hour, billed per second. New accounts get a $50 credit.' (aggregator relaying the vendor's docs)
quoted: 'Each sandbox boots its own guest kernel, sharing nothing with its neighbours.' and, from the page's own description, 'billed per second at $0.04/hr'

record.notes: 1 vCPU / 1 GiB = 0.025 + 0.015 = USD 0.040/hour, which is exactly the vendor's own headline 'billed per second at $0.04/hr', so the two sources agree arithmetically even though only one of them is first party. At 730 h: USD 29.20. What would raise the confidence: a rendered pricing page, which also carries the shape ladder and the session cap.

session_cap.note: hibernate/resume advertised; no cap readable first party

network_out.ports: HTTP(S) and WebSockets through a public URL per exposed port; raw TCP/UDP ingress not stated

record.binding_note: The hourly rate is the wall: USD 0.04/hour for the smallest sandbox is USD 29.20 a month, six times the budget.
